A1.title: Building, updating and reading dicts: key paths and defaults
A1.intro: Building dicts from lists, tuples and text, avoiding KeyError, safe nested access with getVal and getNestedVal, updating by key path, optional fields with defaults.

A2.title: Flattening and walking nested structures
A2.intro: flattenObj and recFlatten, iterating nested layers, de-duplicating nested values, stringifying nested objects.

A3.title: Reshaping lists of dicts: sort, group, dedupe, merge
A3.intro: Sorting by several keys, grouping by a key, de-duplicating, matching and merging two structures.

A4.title: JSON, CSV and Excel in and out
A4.intro: Updating and pruning JSON files, dict to CSV with stable fieldnames, JSON to Excel.

A5.title: pandas: building and reshaping DataFrames
A5.intro: JSON into DataFrames (json_normalize versus a flatten), unnesting list columns, MultiIndex from Excel, splitting and mapping columns, conditional tagging, row and column reshaping.

C1.title: Selecting and navigating HTML
C1.intro: CSS selectors versus find/find_all, :-soup-contains, nth-of-type, sibling and parent hops, attribute selectors, combining criteria, and coping with structure you cannot see in advance. The usual fix is a tighter selector plus select_one with a default.

C2.title: Getting clean text out of tags
C2.intro: get_text with separators and strip, inline tags nested inside text, br handling, whitespace and newlines, aria-hidden spans, separating labels from values, decoding entities.

C3.title: Links, attributes, images and downloads
C3.intro: href and src extraction, relative to absolute URLs with urljoin, lazy-loaded image attributes (data-src), downloading zips, PDFs and images with streaming requests, safe filenames.

C4.title: Tables into DataFrames
C4.intro: pandas.read_html when it works, hand-parsing tables when it does not, rowspan and colspan, header detection, several tables per page, cleaning numbers on the way into a DataFrame.

C5.title: Why is it empty? Debugging None and []
C5.intro: The diagnosis checklist behind every None, [] and AttributeError: wrong selector, content that is not in the HTML (rendered by JavaScript), a blocked response, the wrong URL, or the wrong tag type.

C6.title: Pagination and crawling
C6.intro: Page parameters, next links, finding the total number of pages, queue-based crawling with a visited set and resume, de-duplicating links, polite delays.

C7.title: JavaScript-rendered pages: Selenium and friends
C7.intro: Telling JS-rendered content apart from static HTML, Selenium waits (WebDriverWait and expected conditions), consent and load-more clicks, scrolling, handing page_source to bs4, requests-html, and when to stop and look for the API instead.

C8.title: Hidden APIs and JSON inside script tags
C8.intro: Reading the network tab, replaying XHR calls with requests (headers, payload, cookies), curlconverter, __NEXT_DATA__ and ld+json blocks, JavaScript object literals pulled out of script tags, paginating an API.

C9.title: Blocked requests: headers, Cloudflare, scraping services
C9.intro: Headers and user agents, 403s, Cloudflare challenges and cloudscraper, scraping services as paid escapes, rate limits, the Selenium fallback, and when to stop.

C10.title: Platforms: Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, TikTok, LinkedIn, Glassdoor
C10.intro: Facebook pages through page_source, Twitter through snscrape (which no longer works), YouTube titles and playlists, TikTok, LinkedIn searches, Glassdoor reviews behind a login. Pages as they were in 2022–2023.

C11.title: Saving results: CSV, Excel, PDF, Google Sheets
C11.intro: Rows to CSV and Excel (one sheet or several), JSON out, Google Sheets through gspread or pygsheets, reading a Google Docs table without the API, tables out of PDFs with tabula and pdfplumber.
